"Three-fifty or one-fifty, I won't buy a single apple from you. In your Tazhai Village, I only have one big brother - Lu Ming." It turned out that just a week ago, all the villagers complained that the apple purchase price of two-fifty was too low, so they asked the young man to help contact a big boss, hoping to sell for more money. The young man thought the villagers weren't having it easy and agreed to help them negotiate, trying to sell the village's 500+ tons of apples at three yuan per jin. A few days later, the young man pulled strings to find the biggest apple buyer, Boss Zhang, but Boss Zhang posed a difficult challenge to deliberately make things hard for him - as long as he finished all the liquor and beer on the table, he would buy all 500+ tons from their village. The young man started without a word. Boss Zhang thought he couldn't finish it all, but unexpectedly the young man took it all down in just ten minutes. "Little brother, you're straightforward! I like that. Let's sign the contract now." "Boss Zhang, this three yuan per jin price is really too low. Think about it - just hiring people for bagging and packaging costs at least forty cents more per jin." The condition was he had to drink all 100+ people under the table. Seeing Boss Zhang was also a straightforward person, the young man had no choice but to risk his life and agree with gritted teeth. One bottle after another, who knows how long passed, finally all 100+ people collapsed unconscious. "If you're not satisfied..." The young man's domineering manner successfully conquered Boss Zhang. "You're my Brother Jin! Three-fifty per jin for five million jin of apples. Let's sign the contract now." In the end, he successfully secured the purchase contract, but he drank so much he vomited heavily. The assistant rushed over to take him to the hospital, but the man said no need and happily took out the contract, saying people would come to the village tomorrow to collect the apples. He asked the assistant to help him to the car, but unexpectedly the newly graduated assistant saw the purchase price on the contract was fifty cents higher and became convinced the man was taking kickbacks and profiting from the villagers' price difference. She then indignantly took a photo of the contract and sent it to the villagers' group chat. The next day they rushed to the man's house to demand an explanation. The man had just woken up and thought the villagers came to thank him, so he hurried to greet them, then eagerly said the village's apples had all been sold, and that trucks would come soon to load the goods, telling everyone to go home and prepare. But after hearing this, the villagers immediately said the man was truly heartless, not even sparing the villagers' hard-earned money. The man looked completely confused, not knowing what happened. His father also angrily scolded him, saying if he cheated everyone's money, he wouldn't be forgiven. But just as the man was about to explain, the assistant walked in saying he took kickbacks...

This adorable divine beast is a pet raised by the princess. The beautiful woman before us is Princess Miaoxin. Every day after waking up, she washes her face with these enormous pearls. These pearls contain incredibly magical power that nourishes the skin. On this beautiful Miao Star, a group of fair-skinned, beautiful Pearl People have been born, and their daily work is to salvage pearls. Then they transport them uniformly to outside the palace, and pour these dazzling pearls into troughs. After accumulating a certain quantity, the King and Queen come out. Their daily task is to select the energy... Looking at the Heavenly King Pearl before them, the two are very satisfied. Then the King hands this pearl with enormous energy to his subordinate to pass to the princess. Their day's work ends like this. Next, the princess brings the divine beast and feeds it the pearl. Miao Star's harmonious life is completely shattered at this moment. In an instant, Miao Star descends into chaos. The King quickly organizes people to go to the shelter. The princess, sensing something is wrong, runs quickly toward the palace. Even the precious transformation beasts nearby hide in caves. When the princess reaches the palace, she finds the surroundings completely empty - she has been abandoned by her people. At this time, the King leads a group to a just-crashed warship. Unexpectedly, at this moment, another accident occurs - a huge spaceship rapidly crashes onto the planet, and the strong shockwave immediately...

Just then, the princess arrives late, continuously pounding on the hatch for help. The King can only watch helplessly, unable to do anything. Seeing her father's painful expression, the princess knows...

Accepting reality, amid the King and Queen's crying, she fearlessly turns toward the sea of fire, calmly facing death. Until thirty years later, two long-disappeared Pearl People suddenly appear at the interstellar market, wanting to exchange with a professional thief for the last transformation beast in the universe. The price is the only remaining... in the universe.

The latest 2025 data shows that the number of AIDS infections in Chongqing has approached 120,000, shooting straight up to third place nationwide. Long-term medication, quality of life, and psychological pressure are enormous. Many infected people bear heavy shame and loneliness. Employment, marriage, and social interactions are all subject to invisible discrimination and barriers. What can we do? The answer: don't mistake novelty for freedom. type: Video Browsing; caption: Perhaps, those born in the 90s are truly a very special generation. #nostalgia #90s generation #childhood memories; ocr: Those born in the 1990s still sound so young, yet they have quietly entered another stage of life. Perhaps the childhood memories of hiding to scare their good friends remain vivid. Although called the beat generation, these memories support them as they move forward.; asr: Perhaps those born in the 1990s are truly a special generation. They experienced a childhood without smartphones and fully witnessed the rapid development of the internet. They stand at the intersection of two eras, having seen teachers in person, bulky CRT televisions, and ridden in taxis with manual window cranks. As children, they played 4399 mini-games, and their phones evolved from flip phones all the way to smartphones. They watched cartoons on children's channels and scrolled through short videos late into the night. They went from riding bicycles to riding in cars, from using electric fans to air conditioning. They bought bubble gum for a few cents and cried endlessly for a box of Pokémon cards. After class, they'd put on plastic vampire teeth and hide to scare their friends. Do you still remember that evening when dark clouds suddenly gathered in the sky, heavy rain fell, and the air filled with the smell of rain hitting concrete? This feeling has stayed with many people until now. Those born in the 1990s seem to have caught the last train of the 20th century while becoming the test subjects of the 21st century's rapid development. They witnessed firsthand the simple, warm life in old neighborhoods, and are now experiencing the anxieties of constant change. Many recall how they used to ride bikes to school with classmates in the morning, catch crabs by the river after school, and sit in the courtyard with their grandparents at night, chatting and counting stars. But those days are gone forever, just like some ordinary afternoon when we turned off the children's channel and never turned it back on. We didn't realize then that what we casually turned off was actually our entire childhood. This picture is so small, worth only a few cents, yet it's so large that it carries my entire childhood. "Born in the 1990s" still sounds so young, but today's post-90s generation has quietly entered another phase. Those born in 1990 are 35 years old, those born in 1994 are 31, and even the youngest born in 1999 are already 26. The first batch of post-90s are standing at the threshold of their mid-thirties, while the last batch are hustling through life and striving for their future. The post-90s generation was once called the "lost generation," labeled as non-mainstream, willful, and rebellious. But today, they have emerged from youthful naivety and become a generation shouldering life's heavy responsibilities. They fill their nights with overtime and trade work for stability. They are no longer rebellious but have learned to stay silent, grown accustomed to swallowing their grievances. Facing life's chaos, some say the post-90s have the mindset of 60-year-olds, the pressure of 50-year-olds, the emotions of 40-year-olds, and handle matters like 30-year-olds, yet they lack the innocence of teenagers. Perhaps that innocence has been buried deep in their hearts with time, but it has never disappeared—it has simply transformed into the memories that sustain them as they move forward.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 130, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: True, is_fast_forward_play: True, is_backward_play: True, is_enlarge_play: False

type: Video Browsing; caption: How touching Chinese-style romance is #sense of ceremony #tribute #moved #Yuan Longping; ocr: Chinese-style Romance. A Review of Four Types of Chinese Romance.

First: Ten-Li Street Farewell to Elder Yuan. When the hearse of Academician Yuan Longping, the Father of Hybrid Rice, departed from Xiangya Hospital, the entire city bid farewell to this God of Grain in the most humble way, together fulfilling filial duty! Without organization or call, countless people spontaneously stood by the roadside, clutching white flowers in their hands, tears in their eyes. That day, Changsha flower shops gave away all chrysanthemums for free, and some came carrying rice stalks from the fields, freshly pulled rice plants with fresh soil still clinging to the stalks. This was what Elder Yuan had protected all his life, now becoming gifts to see him off on his final journey. The statue of Elder Yuan holding rice was completely surrounded by a sea of flowers spontaneously offered by students, the water droplets on the petals resembling tears of reluctance. The road the hearse traveled had no traffic police directing, yet spontaneously formed the most solemn procession. Pedestrians stood in the rain, private cars and buses honked in unison, some chased after the convoy, repeatedly calling out "rest in peace." Their voices were dampened by the rain, yet exceptionally clear. University students will remember forever. The rain soaked the banners but couldn't dampen the respect in their eyes. The procession was long, long enough to circle half the city, but compared to the sense of security Elder Yuan cultivated for us, what did this farewell amount to? Elder Yuan once said he had two dreams: the first dream was called "enjoying the cool under rice stalks," the second dream was called "hybrid rice covering the globe." He spent his lifetime being meticulous in the fields, writing his thesis on the land of the motherland. The people mourned Academician Yuan Longping with the deep sorrow of an entire city, seeing you off on your final journey. A national treasure without equal, Elder Yuan eternal.

Second: The Youth Racing Against Flames. In Chongqing in 2022, the once-in-a-century Jinyun Mountain wildfire burned wildly with the wind, the winding mountain roads becoming the greatest obstacle. Fire trucks couldn't get through, firefighting equipment, drinking water, and dry rations piled up at the foot of the mountain, watching helplessly as the flames burned closer, even the air filled with the smell of burning, everyone's hearts twisted into knots. Just then, a rumbling engine sound came from the distance, not rescue vehicles, but a group of young people on motorcycles. Most in their twenties, without uniform clothing, some wearing work pants, some still in short-sleeved T-shirts, faces covered in dust. Wherever supplies needed to go, they went. Those few days, nearly ninety percent of local civilian motorcycles rushed to the disaster area, these young people riding their bikes, shuttling along mountain paths only half a meter wide, knowing only to twist the throttle and charge forward. They weren't professional rescue personnel, but facing the four words "protecting home," they became the bravest knights. A photographer captured a photo that went viral: on the left, raging flames, on the right, countless headlamps of riders and firefighters, one after another, forming a brilliant galaxy. Firelight and lamplight intertwined in the darkness, perfectly forming a large character for "person." Without special effects or design, countless hands and countless lamps wrote the determination that man can conquer nature in the most humble way. Those figures speeding along mountain roads, those clothes soaked with sweat, those hands numbed by engine vibrations, all telling that so-called heroes were never born supermen, but ordinary people willing to stand up in times of crisis. Knights of flame, riding away in a cloud of dust.

Hearing this, the man immediately called the captain, saying he had just heard a car horn. Just as he was about to call the dog over, another cry for help came. Has It Become High-End? #Xiaomi17 #DigitalGadgetGuide #DoubleHolidayChargingFrenzy; ocr: Xiaomi 17 Pro Hands-On Review. Genius design with the delightful rear screen. After 5 years of Xiaomi's push upmarket with an investment of 100 billion, the Xiaomi 17 series has truly succeeded in going premium. There are significant changes in appearance this time, with a truly beautiful texture, larger and more rounded R corners with an 11.5mm radius, similar to the iPhone. Hidden beneath the rounded rectangular DECO module is an 8.6-inch full-screen delightful rear display (ProMax), which is like the external screen on a small foldable. The playability and emotional value of this screen are truly maxed out. Personalization allows you to raise many cute pets and display your favorite pets on the rear screen. These cute pets aren't just simple animation loops, but react realistically based on the phone's status. When listening to music, it puts on headphones; when you make a heart gesture at it, it makes one back, as if it can see you—the emotional value is indescribable. Push notifications can also be displayed on the rear screen for food delivery, ride-hailing, etc. When dynamic notification scenarios are triggered, the rear screen automatically stays on to display service information for easy viewing at any time. Travel assistant, phone calls, clock, Didi, JD.com, Taobao, Super Xiaoai ticketing—notifications can be viewed directly on the rear screen. Most importantly, it can serve as a viewfinder for recording and photography, allowing you to see the composition directly when taking photos or videos. There's also this rear screen game shell. Whoever developed this feature must be a post-80s generation person—they really understand our emotional value. Angry Birds, parkour, fighter jets, Snake—there are many classic games that post-80s love to play. I could play with this thing all day. I have to say Xiaomi's designers are truly geniuses. The screen viewing experience on the 17 Pro Max is incredibly detailed, with super pixels and sub-pixel count reaching 9.38 million, close to the sub-pixel count of a 2K screen, with each pixel having independent RGB sub-pixels. Moreover, the screen shows very uniform color and brightness from any viewing angle. In terms of display and brightness, the screen brightness adjusts automatically, with sunlight mode automatically adjusting brightness in strong light environments to prevent the screen from being too dim. The screen supports full DC dimming and 2160Hz high-frequency dimming. There's also circular polarized light eye protection, which reduces blue light damage by adjusting screen color and texture. When the 17 Pro's brightness is turned to the lowest at night, it's still much brighter than before—it's the brightest generation I've used at night, almost blinding me. After Teacher Li used the iPhone 17 Pro, he said it was very glaring at night, but using the Xiaomi 17 Pro was very comfortable—the value of 1 nit is evident. From then on, wherever he went, enthusiastic Guizhou locals would either bring gifts or present him with banners of commendation. The hot breath a penguin exhales instantly turns into ice, just in the time it takes to close a window. As a result, his head also freezes solid in an instant. But what's even more outrageous is that the cold wind here is utterly unrestrained, carelessly blowing people into the icy wilderness. Even when the door is firmly sealed with wooden boards, the cold wind will blow it out through the window. Seeing how furious the little penguin is, this time he directly takes nails to nail down the bed legs. The extreme cold not only freezes the alarm clock into a huge block of ice, but even the fireplace turns into an ice sculpture. He was ready to light a fire for warmth, but unexpectedly, the coal in the bucket has been completely used up. With no other choice, he can only go directly to his neighbor Ergou's house and without a word prepares to borrow some coal from here. However, Ergou doesn't even have enough coal for himself, so how could he easily give it to him? So he immediately grabs him and pulls him back, pours the coal back into the bucket, then puts the penguin outside the door and kicks him straight back home. With no other option, the little penguin can only burn books for warmth. Just then, an advertisement for a fur coat catches his eye. If he could have one, why would he worry about not being able to withstand the severe cold? So he immediately rushes to the address. Through the door crack, he sees the dazzling array of genuine leather coats and quietly sneaks in from the basement. However, he doesn't notice at all the sign hanging inside warning of a vicious dog. He digs open a hole in the floor, then puts on a carefully selected fox fur coat. Unexpectedly, the next second he runs right into Ergou. Before leaving, he doesn't forget to taunt him. Ergou says he's never seen such an arrogant penguin before. So as soon as the little penguin gets home, Ergou snatches the fur back. The little penguin refuses to give up. This time he sets his sights on a silver-gray coat. Ergou immediately blocks the hole, ready to toy with him a bit. Unexpectedly, the little penguin cleverly dodges with a swift move. Although Ergou pursues fiercely, he still stretches out his long arm to grab it. The unwilling little penguin this time sets his mind on a bearskin coat, but unexpectedly walks right into a trap. To prevent similar incidents from happening again, Ergou locks up all the coats in anger. The little penguin hurriedly looks around and, finding it truly empty, is about to leave in disappointment. But unexpectedly, there's still one piece. However, he doesn't know this is Ergou's tail. Ergou is speechless at his actions. He immediately pulls out his tail and runs back, but unexpectedly the little penguin has taken a liking to his tail. Hiding in the shadows with scissors ready to ambush, but unexpectedly the little penguin's movement is still a step too slow. Then the little penguin immediately tries again, but unexpectedly Ergou takes a bottle and puts his tail inside. Seeing how unwilling the little penguin is, he quickly takes the bottle away, and so an extreme tug-of-war over the tail begins. The little penguin quickly pins down his tail, but how could Ergou let him succeed easily? Seeing Ergou cover his tail with something, the unwilling little penguin continues to make trouble. But unexpectedly, when the axe comes down, the blade actually curls. It turns out Ergou installed an iron pipe on his tail. The little penguin cleverly removes it and plans to use the same trick again, but unexpectedly Ergou makes a hole and hides his tail. The little penguin unwillingly sneaks to the basement, takes haircutting tools and charges them up. Seeing this, Ergou immediately guesses his intention, so he uses rope to make something that looks like a tail. But just as he's waiting to watch the show, he doesn't know the little penguin has already secretly shaved off all his tail fur. Finally, with no other traps, Xiao Hei dared to approach the cage and sprinkled fresh human blood from a bottle on his master's head. At the instant it approaches its prey, it opens its giant mouth at nearly a 90-degree angle, swallowing 220 tons of seawater along with massive amounts of marine life. At this moment, the throat pleats of the blue whale rapidly expand, and its body size instantly doubles. Its originally elegant streamlined body instantly swells into a plump tadpole shape. After completing the engulfment, it filters out the seawater through its baleen plates, swallowing millions of krill into its belly. According to statistics, an adult blue whale must consume four tons of food daily to maintain its basic energy requirements. When the food in its stomach is less than two tons, it experiences intense hunger. To fill its belly, the blue whale dives into waters 30 to 40 meters deep. Once it discovers traces of food, it opens its abyssal giant mouth to devour creatures within a radius of several dozen meters. As a marine mammal, the blue whale still retains the characteristic of breathing with lungs, and therefore needs to surface regularly for air. It sprays water columns over ten meters high from its blowhole, appearing particularly conspicuous on the open sea. Even more astonishing is that blue whale calves are eight meters long at birth, weighing a full 3,500 kilograms. Moreover, the growth rate of the young is extremely remarkable, gaining 90 to 100 kilograms per day. All of this is thanks to the mother's nutrient-rich milk. It's just that the price of all this is too heavy.; asr: In the mahjong parlor, Zhao Fanghua's luck was running high. With a crisp call of "Hu!", a contented smile spread across her fair face. However, she failed to notice that across the table, her neighbor Xiao Pang's sticky, malicious eyes clung to her like flies, lingering on her body as he played absentmindedly. During every interval between drawing and discarding tiles, those shifty, rat-like eyes would greedily roam over her. Taking advantage of the moment when everyone was shuffling tiles, he quickly snatched the house key Zhao Fanghua had left at the corner of the table. The night was dreamlike, and all was silent. When Zhao Fanghua was awakened from her sleep by the slight sound of the door lock turning, a dark figure had already silently appeared at the foot of her bed. Fear instantly gripped her heart. She clutched the blanket tightly, her voice trembling as she demanded to know how he got in. The shadow approached—it was Xiao Pang. He didn't answer, but instead confessed his feelings in a nauseating tone, saying how he had fallen for her at first sight and thought about her day and night. "I've liked you for so long. Get out! How dare you—get out! I really like you. These past few days, I haven't been able to sleep at all. My mind is full of you. Ever since I saw you last time, you're all I can think about." "Get out! Wang Yang, how can you do this? We're both married people with families. What you're doing is wrong to our families. Get out right now, or I'll call the police!" Zhao Fanghua's anger overcame her fear. Xiao Pang's expression changed instantly. He dropped to his knees with a thud, cursing and swearing that he was just confused for a moment, while also using reality to threaten her. "I like you so much, you know? Just forgive me this once. I'm so dizzy. If you call the police, I'll go to jail. What will happen to my child? If you tell Zhao Minglun, he'll beat me to death." These words were like a bucket of ice water dousing Zhao Fanghua's fury and freezing her determination to call the police. Looking at the man crying before her, her heart filled with disgust and struggle. Finally, she just said coldly, "Hand over the key you copied, then disappear immediately." After Xiao Pang left, Zhao Fanghua couldn't sleep all night. That copied key seemed to become a sword hanging over her head. She thought about calling the police, but Xiao Pang's words struck deep. In this world where gossip is fearsome, a woman's reputation is sometimes more important than her innocence itself. A few days later, her husband Zhang Ming, who drove long-haul trucks, came home. Looking at her husband's travel-worn face, Zhao Fanghua wanted to speak several times, but those humiliating words, when they reached her lips, became like burning iron that she couldn't spit out. She chose silence, thinking this storm would pass. However, her silence was seen by Xiao Pang as weakness. A month later, seeing that all was calm, his extinguished criminal intent reignited. That day, Zhao Fanghua had just seen off her husband who was leaving on another business trip. As she turned to close the door, Xiao Pang's figure squeezed in like a ghost, blocking the door with his body and spewing filthy words. Zhao Fanghua was shocked and frightened, lying that her husband would be back soon. But Xiao Pang just sneered, "Who are you fooling? Zhang Ming won't be back for at least ten days to two weeks." Unable to bear it any longer, Zhao Fanghua spat in his face, raised her phone, and screamed hysterically, "If you don't leave, I'll die right in front of you!" Xiao Pang was frightened by her determination and reluctantly retreated. The door was locked heavily, and Zhao Fanghua collapsed on the floor, tears of grievance flooding out. She still didn't dare call the police. She feared her husband wouldn't believe her, and even more, she feared the contemptuous looks from neighbors. Her weakness ultimately brought greater disaster. It turned out that Xiao Pang had insanely made two keys. He tried the same trick again, sneaking into Zhao Fanghua's home late at night. However, this time he miscalculated—Zhang Ming's truck had broken down halfway, and he unexpectedly returned home early. "Who the hell are you? What are you doing in my house?" Zhang Ming's roar exploded in the living room. Xiao Pang panicked and incoherently claimed he had entered the wrong door. But Zhang Ming immediately spotted the set of keys in his hand that were identical to their own. Seeing things going badly, Xiao Pang pushed Zhang Ming aside and ran out, disappearing into the night. He repeated this operation continuously. Only after dozens of gold bars were coated with the pungent chili water did he feel confident he could evade the police dogs' sense of smell when passing through security. Soon, a barefoot old woman appeared at the train station, hunched over and pushing a baby carriage as cover. At the bottom of the carriage were the gold bars that had been treated with chili water. She put on a kind expression and went to the ticket counter to buy a ticket. The ticket seller stared at her aged face, not connecting this figure with the wanted poster on the wall at all. After getting the ticket, the fugitive quickly scanned for the passage with the least foot traffic and hurried forward. Just as the exit came into view, a patrol soldier appeared in sight. The military dog beside him suddenly became agitated, its nose fixed on the bottom of the baby carriage. His heart tightened, and he immediately pretended to be frightened by the dog. Seeing this, the patrol captain rushed over, but far from suspecting this trembling old person, he was instead worried that the military dog had disturbed the child in the carriage. While repeatedly apologizing to the old woman, he helpfully assisted her onto the platform. The man passed through security smoothly this way. But just as he was about to board the train, another patrol soldier passed by with a military dog, and that dog also started barking frantically at the baby carriage. The captain, hearing the commotion, rushed over and immediately sensed something was wrong—dogs wouldn't target the same person for no reason. So he stepped forward to question them. The person tried to remain calm and explain, but before he could finish speaking, the captain had already lifted the blanket under the baby, and a whole package was revealed. Just as the captain was about to reach for it, the man suddenly kicked out violently. The captain immediately doubled over in pain on the ground, and his behavior instantly drew the attention of other soldiers. type: Video Browsing; caption: Magical Wheat Seedlings #AnimationExplanation; ocr: The farmer looked at the heavy harvest in his hands, and the fireplace always burned with purchased firewood. The farmer had just reached the edge of the field when he became exhausted, and indeed stopped working, and before long was completely submerged. It fell down and crushed him to death beneath it.; asr: A farmer discovered a wheat seedling still growing in a field of dead wheat. Overjoyed, he immediately fetched a hoe to weed and loosen the soil around it, then secured the seedling with rope and branches to prevent it from falling over. To make watering more convenient, he even cut down trees and built a small wooden hut nearby. Even his pets were called to help. After some time, the farmer's efforts were rewarded—the seedling began to thrive under his care. However, the good times didn't last. One night, a violent rainstorm struck. Seeing the seedling in peril amid the wind and rain, the farmer grew anxious and rushed over to reinforce the ropes. He dug ditches to drain the accumulated water, and finally brought his own sleeping mat to wrap the seedling tightly. The farmer guarded the seedling all night, standing in the wind and rain. The next morning, after the rain cleared, something astonishing happened—the seedling suddenly grew rapidly, instantly transforming into a towering tree. Its dense canopy was laden with layers of wheat ears, completely beyond what a wheat plant should look like. The farmer was overjoyed and continued weeding and loosening the soil, anticipating the harvest. By afternoon, golden wheat grains fell like raindrops. Holding the heavy harvest in his hands and immersed in the fragrance of wheat, the farmer was extremely happy. They sang and danced in this golden rain, celebrating this rare harvest. Soon the wheat grains piled up like mountains. It took the farmer several days to bag everything and transport it home. Afterward, he took some grain to town to exchange for money and used this wealth to live a new life. His table now had fish and meat, he wore clothes he couldn't afford before, and even in the cold winter, firewood always burned in his fireplace. He ate his fill and slept, slept and ate again—his days were quite comfortable. However, after prolonged ease, the farmer gradually became lazy. Looking at the wheat tree covered in snow outside his window, he no longer cared for it as meticulously as before. He did nothing all winter until spring arrived. When the snow melted and temperatures rose, the farmer stepped outside for the first time, his belly now protruding. Only at his pet's urging did he reluctantly shoulder the wheat seeds and head toward the field. But due to long-term lack of exercise, the farmer was exhausted before even reaching the field. Then he saw that the withered wheat tree had sprouted new buds. Instantly excited, he rushed forward and embraced it, even fantasizing about never having to work again and having endless food. With this thought, he threw down his tools and returned home. He no longer wanted to work. He even patted the dog's head and said working was impossible for a lifetime—following it, even lying flat, one could eat well. The pets heard this boast and indeed stopped working too. By summer, the scorching sun baked the earth. The field under the wheat tree cracked and was overgrown with weeds. The farmer and his pets still slept comfortably at home, and no one was willing to weed or water anymore. When harvest season came and all the stored food was gone, the farmer finally brought burlap sacks and the animals to the field, eagerly preparing to harvest the grain. He skillfully beat the tree trunk with a wooden stick, and the next second, a large amount of wheat grains fell like raindrops, soon burying him completely. The delighted farmer didn't notice the danger at all. Fortunately, the animals helped him climb out of the wheat pile. But the farmer's face still beamed with smiles—after all, so much grain was enough for him to enjoy wealth and glory for a lifetime, never having to worry about food again. Just as he was happily daydreaming, he accidentally swallowed some wheat grains and nearly vomited from disgust. Sensing something was wrong, he quickly scooped up a handful of grains and looked carefully, discovering they were mixed with quite a bit of black impurities and tasted even worse than excrement. This terrified the farmer, who quickly escaped from the wheat pile. When he looked at the wheat tree again, his eyes were full of regret and unwillingness. He couldn't accept that after waiting so long, this was the result. Enraged, he forcefully grabbed the wooden stick and struck the wheat tree, which then fell and crushed him beneath it.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 8, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: False, is_fast_forward_play: False, is_backward_play: False, is_enlarge_play: False

Due to the discovery of multiple looting pits requiring protective development, we stepped forward and quietly asked the visitors a few questions.; asr: I accidentally discovered an ancient tomb from the Warring States period. I thought that after finishing this job, I could retire wealthy, but I didn't expect problems to arise during the selling phase. Everyone in our entire operation was caught by the police in one sweep. After the public security department completed their investigation, we were sentenced to life imprisonment. However, the appearance of a mysterious old man led to my inexplicable release, simply because he wanted me to explore a thousand-year-old tomb and rescue those missing experts. "I don't know you, why are you looking for me?" "Fifth Master, it doesn't matter if you don't know me, but I know you. Your reputation in your circle is absolutely resounding. Oh, let me introduce myself. My name is Zhang Yi, affiliated with the Ministry of State Security." Before he finished speaking, my heart sank with a thud. My mind buzzed, and my body stood up uncontrollably. The mysterious man smiled as he watched my reaction, gesturing for me to sit back down. "I heard Fifth Master is a straightforward person, so I don't want to beat around the bush. Let's get straight to the point. Now there's an opportunity for you to leave this place. Are you interested?" "What do you want me to do? What can I do? Do you want me to rob tombs for the country? This is fucking ridiculous." "Don't be hasty. We discovered an ancient tomb in Northeast China. Because multiple robbery holes were found, it needs to be developed and protected, and it has already been approved. Are you willing to go and provide some necessary technical support?" "I'm afraid it's not that simple. What's really going on? Just tell me straight." "That ancient tomb has problems. Three experts who entered successively never came back out. To this day, we don't know if they're dead or alive. Fifth Master is definitely one of the few experts in this field, so you're the first person we thought of. Of course, you can refuse, and we'll pretend today's conversation never happened." "What do I get out of it?" "Your current status means you're destined to spend your whole life in prison, but we can give you a brand new identity, a legitimate professional title, limited financial support, and a considerable salary." "Tomb raiding isn't as simple as having a meal. I can't do anything alone. I need my people with me. After all, we've been through life and death together for so many years and have developed a rapport that's hard to cultivate." "Time is pressing. Three old experts are in the tomb with their fates unknown. How long will it take you to find those people? Do you know where they all are?" "Same as me, all in prison." "Good. Write me a list right now. We depart in one hour." type: Video Browsing; caption: Lu Zhishen Wreaks Havoc at Peach Blossom Village, Beats Up Little Tyrant Zhou Tong #FastTalkDramaReview #NewWaterMargin; ocr: "Water Margin." Lu Zhishen and Lin Chong watching a shadow play. This is your Grandpa Zhishen right here.; asr: Five pounds of beef with wine, he could drink all night long. His antics shocked everyone around him - this monk not only drank but also ate meat! After a few cups, he started grabbing food with his hands, looking like he wanted to shove the whole dish into his mouth. His eating manner absolutely had the potential to become a viral internet celebrity. The old master watching from the side felt his scalp tingle. "My goodness, Master is truly extraordinary!" "Is this enough?" "The wine and meat are about done, but if we could have another two or three bowls of rice, that would be even better." The old master immediately ordered servants to bring out a large plate of rice, but he still underestimated Lu's appetite. In just two minutes, that full basin of rice was already empty. Lu Zhishen directly picked up the remaining vegetable soup and poured it into the basin, then stirred it clockwise with chopsticks - a fragrant rice bowl was thus made. The steward watching from the side was dumbfounded, thinking this one meal had consumed three days' worth of rations for the household. Fortunately, as the last piece of dried tofu was eliminated, Lu Zhishen finally put down his chopsticks and contentedly wiped his mouth. Seeing this, they quickly ordered the table cleared, fearing he wasn't full yet and would ask for two more basins of rice. The old master finally breathed a sigh of relief and prepared to get up and leave. The old man casually arranged for the master to stay in the side room, noting that if there was any commotion at night, he shouldn't come out to look. "Ah, thank you, master." Lu Zhishen didn't understand - what could happen late at night that a monk couldn't see? So he got up and stopped the master to inquire about the situation. Seeing the master refused to explain, Lu Zhishen's expression immediately changed. "Is it because I ate too much food and disturbed you?" As he spoke, he prepared to take out silver from his bundle to pay for the meal. Unexpectedly, the master quickly stopped him. "This old man usually provides vegetarian meals to monks without hesitation. One more master is nothing, it's just that my daughter is getting married today and there are some troubles." Upon hearing this, Lu Zhishen's face immediately lit up with joy, thinking he could attend a wedding feast tonight. But at the same time he was very puzzled - this was clearly a joyous occasion, so why did he look so worried? At this point, the master reluctantly revealed the reason. It turned out that some time ago, a group of bandits who robbed and violated women came to the estate demanding money. Unexpectedly, they took a fancy to his eighteen-year-old daughter. The bandits threw down twenty taels of gold and a bolt of silk as betrothal gifts, saying they would come tonight to take the young lady away as the mountain stronghold's wife. Lu Zhishen, who had always hated evil, became furious upon hearing this and immediately decided to intervene to stop this marriage. "I learned the skill of arranging marriages from Elder Zhizhen at Mount Wutai," he said. "I can make that bandit chief not marry your daughter and change his mind." But Old Master Liu was full of doubt after hearing this, because those bandits were all ruthless killers - how could mere words persuade them? But Lu Zhishen confidently reassured him, "Old master, don't be afraid. I have my own clever plan to ensure your daughter's safety." That evening, the bandits from Peach Blossom Mountain indeed arrived on time with drums and music. The bandit leader, Little Tyrant Zhou Tong, was even wearing wedding clothes, his face beaming with joy, unable to stop smiling. He couldn't wait to reach the young lady's boudoir, ready to enjoy this precious bride. In the dim candlelight, he groped his way to the red bed. Seeing the wonderful body under the bedding, Zhou Tong's heart leaped with wild joy. He felt through the quilt a few times, and the more he touched, the more his heart itched unbearably. He simply stuck his hand directly into the bedding and groped wildly. "What a big belly! Haha, never mind the big belly, the legs are big too!" A huge iron fist came whistling through the air with the sound of wind, heading straight for his face. "You're asking for it!" Then came another explosive attack. Zhou Tong never expected that on this wedding night, he would be the first to bleed. The commotion in the room drew a group of his men who rushed over aggressively. Lu Zhishen glared at them, and without a word, directly grabbed Zhou Tong who hadn't yet recovered his senses and flung him out. The men, seeing this giant, didn't dare to fight and were scared, running faster than rabbits. Old Master Liu who rushed over was immediately panicked

type: Video Browsing; ocr: An employee took sick leave for foot pain, but their WeChat Sports step count exceeded 16,000 that day. The company dismissed them for absenteeism. The court ruled the company's termination of the employment contract was unlawful and ordered payment of 118,779 yuan in compensation. According to Red Star News on October 24, an employee of a company in Jiangsu took sick leave multiple times for back pain and foot pain. The company discovered that on the day of foot pain, the employee's WeChat Sports step count exceeded 16,000, and subsequently dismissed them for absenteeism. The two parties went to court over this matter. The first-instance court found that based on the outpatient medical records and diagnostic certificates provided by the employee, the facts of seeking treatment and rest for back pain and right foot pain were established, and the relevant diagnosis was not based solely on personal statements. Given that numerous factors can affect WeChat Sports step counts, the company's use of this as grounds for determining absenteeism was insufficient. In conclusion, the first-instance court ruled that the company's termination of the employment contract lacked factual basis, constituted unlawful termination, and ordered payment of 118,779 yuan in compensation. 1.6 billion people worldwide have been deceived by the Tathagata Buddha. The night Sun Wukong returned after killing the Six-Eared Macaque, Tang Sanzang secretly recited the Tight-Fillet Spell, but the monkey before him showed no reaction. I, pretending to sleep nearby, witnessed everything. From that day on, I never called him "Brother Monkey" again, and Master never recited the spell again. In the blink of an eye, thousands of years passed. Master and I outwardly submitted to our titles and secretly became Buddhas.

For a thousand years on Spirit Mountain, I served as the Altar Cleanser, my daily work being to consume the offerings presented to Buddha. All the gods and Buddhas laughed at me, saying I was worthless, that even after fourteen years of scripture-seeking I couldn't change my gluttonous nature. They didn't know I wasn't eating offerings—I was consuming resentment. I wasn't waiting for the next vegetarian meal; I was waiting for an opportunity to overturn the Three Realms.

A thousand years ago, after the Western Journey, we four disciples were granted titles on Spirit Mountain. The Victorious Fighting Buddha, Sun Wukong, stood before Master in golden armor, his face full of joy at achieving enlightenment. Junior Brother Sha and I stood solemnly on either side. But I saw Master—the Sandalwood Merit Buddha—looking at Brother Monkey with eyes devoid of any light, his aged face showing an unfathomable sorrow I'd never seen before.

Late that night in the monastery, I pretended to be drunk. Master approached Brother Monkey. His shadow stretched long in the moonlight. After a long silence, I heard his voice, light as wind—he was reciting the Tight-Fillet Spell. Once, twice, three times. I knew what Master was doing—verifying, making final confirmation. Yet Wukong just stood there quietly with a puzzled expression: "Master, what are you chanting? Your disciple doesn't understand." No reaction whatsoever.

The courtyard fell deathly silent. Master softly said, "Nothing. Your master just wanted to look at you again." Wukong smiled and scratched his head: "Master, I'll accompany you every day from now on." Master said nothing more, just slowly turned away. Tears silently fell from his aged cheeks.

In that moment, I understood everything. After the True and False Monkey King ordeal, the one who accompanied us to the Western Heaven wasn't my Brother Monkey at all. That lawless one who dared fight Heaven, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven—he was already dead. We had brought an imposter, a puppet manufactured by Spirit Mountain, to the end and received this laughable title.

Master's tears were for Brother Monkey, for himself, for this fourteen-year deception. And I was the only witness. From that day, I was no longer Marshal Tianpeng or Zhu Bajie. I became a gluttonous, lazy, lustful Altar Cleanser who could never amount to anything—this was my protective coloring. In this massive web of fame and profit, a harmless waste could live longest and see most clearly.

Master changed too, becoming the most devout Sandalwood Merit Buddha, daily expounding dharma, radiating Buddha-light. He and the Victorious Fighting Buddha were like two parallel lines, silently operating on separate tracks for a thousand years—until today.

Spirit Mountain gathered ten thousand Buddhas for another grand dharma assembly. I sat in the lowest position, yawning boredly. When the dharma discussion segment arrived, Master slowly stood up. Only I understood when he mentioned "true self" and "dharma nature"—this was the code we'd set a thousand years ago. The time had come.

I maintained my drowsy appearance but spoke loudly: "Buddha, I don't understand all that. I only know when hungry, you eat. This hunger is the true self. Seeing offerings makes me want to eat—this desire is dharma nature. Eating brings comfort. Who cares about true self and dharma nature? Filling the belly is what's real." All the Buddhas laughed at me. But Master slowly sat back down. He understood my answer: "Eating brings comfort" meant the plan could begin. After enduring for a thousand years, it was time to release this pent-up anger.

The next day, Master's decree arrived: I was to prepare offerings. The secret order hidden in Buddha-light read: Netherworld Fire Prison. To rescue Brother Monkey, we first had to break the Ten Thousand Buddha Prison. The only weakness required extremely evil artifacts scattered across the Three Realms. The first was the Netherworld Fire Prison of Mount Luofeng, guarded by the Six Heavenly Ghost Kings. Sending a worthless fool like me was the perfect cover.

First: Li Weigang, a Man of Benevolence and Integrity

A single product promotion mishap allowed countless people to recognize the delicate sense of responsibility hidden beneath this man's rugged exterior. He is the only person whose product promotion failure earned praise from People's Daily, and the only man who moved anti-fraud bloggers to tears.

The incident stemmed from an ordinary beef promotion. With the genuine intention of benefiting his fans, Li Weigang carefully selected a product, only to be exposed by netizens and suffer a complete failure. Investigation revealed that the brand had played a bait-and-switch trick—displaying genuine products during the livestream but shipping inferior substitutes.

According to insiders, Li Weigang earned 750,000 yuan from this promotion. Following the tenfold compensation rule, he owed 7.5 million yuan. By industry convention, most influencers would choose to deflect blame or even disappear. But Li Weigang did the opposite. He immediately stepped forward without a single excuse, faced the problem head-on, and solemnly apologized to all consumers: "I really wanted to bring everyone quality products, but I naively trusted the distributor's promises. It's my fault for betraying everyone's trust. I sincerely apologize to everyone."

He then paid the 7.5 million yuan compensation out of his own pocket first, and after resolving consumer issues, pursued legal action against the brand. Overnight, Li Weigang became affectionately known as "Brother Compensation," but those 7.5 million yuan lost in money won back trust and respect that cannot be measured in numbers.

Li Weigang's kindness extends far beyond daring to compensate. Last December, Li Weigang planned to lease a fish pond. The owner was a young man who quoted 5,080 yuan. This oddly specific number aroused Brother Gang's curiosity. After conversation, he learned the young man's parents had both died, the fish pond was their only inheritance, and 5,080 yuan was his tuition for one semester—his only means to continue his education.

Upon learning the truth, Li Weigang felt deeply moved. He immediately decided to help this sensible young man, even at a loss to himself. He hired workers to help catch the fish. From the ten-acre pond, they caught over 4,000 pounds of fish, expected to sell for over 17,000 yuan.

Just when everyone thought Brother Gang could finally shed his "Compensation Brother" label and even make a small profit, his actions once again commanded respect. He transferred 17,666 yuan to the young man and covered all labor costs. Before leaving, he sincerely told the boy: "I can't profit from your money. Whatever the fish sell for, I'll give it all to you, because you still have to work summer jobs and earn tuition. I hope you'll put more energy into your studies. Summer jobs are quite hard and tiring, and you're only 19 years old."

As netizens said, Brother Gang's livestream might fail, but his character never will.

Second: Guardian of the Winter Cold, Dongbei Guaige

"Add oil, Oli Gei!" Some wait for him to fall, but he waits for his winter. The internet's only seasonal celebrity, he looks like a troll and speaks with down-to-earth enthusiasm, yet with his spirit of never bowing to life, he became a real man rated perfect by millions.

Compared to other influencers with luxury cars and mansions, he remains destitute. He must care for his father who cannot care for himself and accompany his brother with congenital intellectual disabilities. The family's entire burden rests on his shoulders alone. Yet even so, he has never exploited misery for traffic. Among thousands of published works, there's not a single hard advertisement, not one instance of hype, and no scripted content.

Every dawn, Dongbei Guaige streams on time—no PK battles, no product promotions, still destitute. Until one day when his father suddenly fell ill requiring enormous medical expenses, Dongbei Guaige opened the tipping function for the first time during his livestream.

That night, this man who never bowed his head knelt on the ground with tears in his eyes, thanking every netizen who extended help. As soon as the medical expenses were collected, he immediately closed the tipping function. He said: "I took your money to save a life, so I cannot take your money to get rich."

Before this, he had been a teacher for ten years, worked construction sites, and even collected garb

You just sent out a mass text asking to borrow 1,000 yuan, but unexpectedly received 100 million directly. Looking at the incoming payment notifications on your phone, your face instantly showed utter shock. 3 million, 5 million, 50 million—wait, what? I only asked to borrow 1,000 yuan for living expenses. What are you all transferring? Are you all this rich? Wait, I'm not related to them at all, don't even know them. A while ago, several strangers somehow got your contact info, not only added you on WeChat but also bragged that you could message them if you needed anything—there's nothing they couldn't handle.

Then you received messages from those people on your phone: "Kid Lu, don't treat our money as money, spend it freely, spend it hard. Help us spend this money within a month." "Kid Lu, use this 100 million to chase girls. Spend it all and we'll give you the next reward." "If you don't spend it all in a month... you don't want lives on your hands, do you?" Looking at your phone screen, you're completely confused. Why would these strangers who aren't related to you transfer money? How did they get your bank account number? It must be criminals trying to frame you with dirty money. No wonder they kept emphasizing "lives"—they're definitely looking for a scapegoat. With this thought, you took a cab straight to the police station. You must turn them all in. Looking for a scapegoat? Ha, they didn't expect me, Lu Xiao...

As soon as you entered, you got straight to the point: "Officer, I want to report a crime. A group of lunatics added me and sent me 100 million. I seriously suspect this is dirty money. I suggest you investigate their last three generations." The officer replied impatiently, "Who would give you 100 million for nothing? Why don't they give me 100 million? The police station serves the people, not a place for your games. Leave immediately."

Seeing the officer didn't believe you, you got anxious and slammed your phone on the desk, showing your bank balance and transfer records, saying excitedly, "Look, it really is 100 million. Why would I lie to you?" Seeing those glaring numbers...

"Holy crap, someone really sent you 100 million!" A police officer who looked like a leader quickly regained composure and said seriously, "Investigate! Call the bank immediately to check these people's transaction records, see if it's related to gambling, drugs, or fraud..."

After some busy work at the station, the chief finally told you, "Young man, the accounts that transferred money to you all have legitimate sources of income, no account theft, they voluntarily sent you money. You can really spend it if they want you to. You could even donate it, though if you want to donate to the Red Cross, I'd advise you to think carefully before deciding."

Coming out of the police station, you were stunned—this 100 million could actually be spent with peace of mind. You thought to yourself: Rich people think they have too much money, but you, Lu Xiaochen, don't think so. You immediately opened your dad's WeChat and directly transferred 50 million to your father: "Dad, some lunatics just sent me 100 million. I know you're poor too, take this money..."

A simple, kind face appeared in your mind—your father on the day he sent you to college: "Son, our family is dirt poor. You need to work hard to earn money. Your dad and mom are ordinary people this lifetime..." Thinking of this, you used your hand...

"The old guy was so poor but raised me, it really wasn't easy. Hope he won't be scared receiving 50 million all at once."

At this time, on a remote island, there stood a palace. The palace looked ordinary, but if...

To take care of their welfare, I prepare a lavish buffet dinner every night with a 150 yuan standard. A new employee complained online saying "What's the use of this? The benefits and treatment were beyond question. When they worked overtime at night, I provided them with a 150 yuan per person buffet. I was confused - the order wasn't finished yet, where was I? "Your company's employee meal standards are so high, yet people are complaining. I think you've just spoiled them. You should check it out quickly, it's spreading all over the internet." Alarmed, I quickly went online to check and found that someone had photographed the company's products and posted: "It's all formalism. Working overtime exhausts me to death. I just want money. Instead of giving me a 150 yuan meal allowance, I'd rather have 100 yuan cash. Besides, who can eat so much greasy food at night? The country is encouraging..." Looking at the comments, more than half actually supported him. I couldn't help but shake my head and called my assistant to find out who it was. That face floated into my mind. Soon the assistant found out it was the intern Shen Youchu. "Boss, I've already told him to delete the post. I thought this was just the beginning, but the next day I saw three dishes and a soup with a note beside them: "Meal fee: 25 yuan." I stared at that note for a full half minute, my mind racing. Three dishes and a soup, meat and vegetables, beautifully presented, with an enticing aroma—at a restaurant outside, this would cost at least 50. At 25, it was worth it. I picked up my chopsticks and grabbed a piece of glistening braised pork. It was so delicious I almost swallowed my tongue. After eating, I burped contentedly. Looking at the greasy dishes, laziness took over. I experimentally piled them in the sink without washing them, just to test this roommate's limits. The next morning, I was woken by the slight clinking of pots and pans. I tiptoed to the kitchen door and saw the dishes in the sink washed spotless and neatly stacked. Next to them was another note in ordinary black pen: "Dishwashing fee: 5 yuan per time, settled at month's end." I was furious. Really? In my 20-plus years of life, this was the first time I'd met such a principled ghost. My competitive spirit was fully aroused. Rules, huh? Fine! I deliberately left a garbage bag full of trash by the door, blocking half the path. If you're so capable, throw it out for me. The next day, the garbage bag was gone, and a sticky note on the door read: "Errand fee: 10 yuan." I worked late into the night and fumbled in the dark to turn on the light. Suddenly, the living room light turned on by itself, soft and not glaring. Something in my heart softened for a moment, then a note floated down from the lampshade: "Left the light on for you. If I threw a sock on the floor, she'd worry and I'd get so angry I'd jump and curse at the air: "Is it any of your business? You iron-fisted miser who's controlling even in death!" Then words would appear on the mirror: "Right back at you." She was even a bit tsundere. At least I never ate instant noodles again. At least in this cold big city, there was someone who would leave a light on for me. But good times didn't last. The chill of capitalism still reached me, a small worker. A cold email and a few lines of impersonal text froze the meager salary I'd earned through two hours of daily commuting. I don't know how long I cried.
